title: A Positive Dispersion Optimum for the Rounded Sample Mean: Sufficiency and Necessity of Finite Variance
summary: A continuous quantity, observable only after nearest-lattice rounding, is estimated by the mean of $n$ rounded readings of an imperfect instrument. Averaged over the position of the true value within a rounding cell, the mean-squared error of this estimator is a function of one dimensionless parameter: the pre-rounding standard deviation $s$, measured in cell widths. A perfectly repeatable instrument ($s=0$) returns the same rounded value on every reading, so averaging provides no additional information; its cell-averaged error is the rounding floor $1/12$.
